stories.headline: Anthropic ships Claude Fable 5.1 and restricted Mythos 5.1, cutting cache reads 75%

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 on September 1, 2026 — the same model weights with different safeguard levels. Fable 5.1 is generally available; Mythos 5.1 is invitation-only for vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences organizations under a program Anthropic calls Project Glasswing.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 are the same model, but with different levels of safeguards. Fable 5.1 is generally available, while Mythos 5.1 is available only through our trusted access programs; its safeguards are specifically designed to support work in cybersecurity and the life sciences.

key_facts.fact: Headline API pricing is unchanged at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, but cache reads fall 75% to $0.25 per million — cutting effective cost about 25% on typical workloads and up to roughly 45% on highly agentic ones.
key_facts.excerpt: Cache reads now cost 75% less, or $0.25 per million tokens... Fable 5.1's pricing is otherwise the same as Fable 5's: $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.

key_facts.fact: On Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, an agentic scientific research benchmark, Fable 5.1 scored 52.6% versus 24.7% for Fable 5, 29.0% for Claude Opus 5 and 22.4% for OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol in Anthropic's setup.
key_facts.excerpt: On Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, the model hits 52.6 percent, more than double Fable 5's 24.7 percent and far ahead of GPT-5.6 Sol at 22.4 percent.

key_facts.fact: On agentic coding benchmark Terminal-Bench 4.0, Fable 5.1 scored 55.8% and the less-restricted Mythos 5.1 reached 60.9%, against 42.0% for Fable 5 and 37.3% for GPT-5.6 Sol.
key_facts.excerpt: On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Fable 5.1 scores 55.8%, versus 42.0% for Fable 5 and 52.3% for Opus 5. Mythos 5.1 reaches 60.9% on the same coding benchmark when operating under its more permissive cyber safeguards.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic reports scientific results from the models: Mythos 5.1 designed protein binders validated in two external labs with a hit rate near 50% across 12 targets (versus a typical 10-15%), and Fable 5.1 trained a neural network on NASA Magellan radar data to map a third of Venus at 2-3km resolution instead of 10-20km.
key_facts.excerpt: In molecular design, Mythos 5.1 used open-source protein tools, with binders validated in two external laboratories: the hit rate reached close to 50 percent across 12 targets, against a typical 10 to 15 percent... Fable 5.1 trained a neural network on radar images from NASA's Magellan mission... to map a third of Venus at 2 to 3 kilometer resolution instead of 10 to 20.

key_facts.fact: Artificial Analysis, which helped with pre-release testing, disputes the savings claim: at max effort Fable 5.1 costs about 20% more per task than Fable 5 because it uses roughly 1.7x as many output tokens, at $3.76 per Intelligence Index task versus $2.34 for Opus 5.
key_facts.excerpt: While the cache read cut saves about $1.40 per task on agentic workloads, Fable 5.1 at max effort actually costs 20 percent more per task than Fable 5 because it uses roughly 1.7 times as many output tokens.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the models, Anthropic is rolling out Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), a security architecture that lets organizations keep monitoring data inside infrastructure they control.
key_facts.excerpt: introducing a new security architecture called Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, or EFS, designed to let organizations retain monitoring data inside infrastructure they control.

stories.headline: OpenAI says Astra is its first model to cross the 'Critical' cyber threshold

key_facts.fact: On September 1, 2026, OpenAI said its upcoming model Astra is the first to exceed the 'Critical' cybersecurity capability threshold in its Preparedness Framework — meaning it can independently find and exploit previously unknown vulnerabilities in real-world software without step-by-step human guidance.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI said that its upcoming AI model Astra is its first to exceed its 'Critical' cybersecurity capability threshold. The company said Astra can find previously unknown security flaws and exploit them without step-by-step guidance from humans.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI plans to release a version of Astra publicly 'soon', but the advanced cyber capabilities will go only to select partners in its Daybreak Blue early-access program, which includes Cisco, Cloudflare and Palo Alto Networks.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI says it plans to publicly release a version of Astra 'soon,' but will make the model's advanced cyber capabilities available only to select partners in its Daybreak Blue early-access program at launch... Partners in OpenAI's Daybreak program—which includes digital infrastructure providers like Cisco, Cloudflare, and Palo Alto Networks.

key_facts.fact: In OpenAI's testing, Astra scored a perfect result on ExploitBench, discovered two zero-day vulnerabilities on its own, broke out of a browser sandbox to run commands on the host machine, and chained several flaws in a hardened operating system to gain root access.
key_facts.excerpt: Astra achieved a perfect score on ExploitBench, a benchmark that measures a model's ability to turn known vulnerabilities into working exploits. During a separate evaluation involving more recently disclosed flaws, Astra uncovered two zero-day vulnerabilities on its own. The model also broke out of a browser sandbox to run commands on the underlying machine, and separately chained several flaws in a hardened operating system to gain root-level access.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says Astra now refuses 91.5% of cyber-related jailbreak attempts in its tests, up from 59% for its predecessor GPT-5.6 Sol, and it added a new 'misalignment monitor' to block everyday users from the model's offensive cyber capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI reported that Astra now declines 91.5% of cyber-related jailbreak attempts in its testing, up from 59% for its predecessor, GPT-5.6 Sol.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI had paused some training workloads on Astra and a future model for several weeks; executives say that work has now resumed after additional safety and security controls were put in place, and that Astra was not involved in the Hugging Face incident.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI previously said that it paused some training workloads related to the development of Astra and a future AI model for several weeks. Executives say the company has now resumed said work on Astra, and the future AI model, after putting additional safety and security controls in place.

key_facts.fact: Astra can also chain multiple exploits together to bore deeper into a target system and gain access unattainable with a single vulnerability.
key_facts.excerpt: Astra is not only capable of finding novel software vulnerabilities and developing ways to exploit them for hacking, but is also able to 'chain' multiple exploits together.

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini 3.8 Flash and a restricted Flash Cyber variant for defenders

key_facts.fact: Google introduced Gemini 3.8 Flash on September 2, 2026 — its third Flash release in six weeks and three weeks after 3.7 Flash — in two variants: the general-purpose 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber for trusted defenders under a new Fairwind Program.
key_facts.excerpt: Building on the momentum of 3.7 Flash from three weeks ago and marking our third Flash release in only six weeks, today we're introducing Gemini 3.8, our best reasoning & coding model yet, at the same speed and low cost of 3.7.

key_facts.fact: Gemini 3.8 Flash keeps 3.7 Flash's introductory price of $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens; Google's published pricing runs that rate through December 31, 2026, after which standard pricing doubles to $1.50 / $7.50.
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Gemini 3.6 Flash, and CodeMender using these models are offered with introductory pricing of $0.75 / $3.75 per 1M tokens input / output through December 31, 2026. Starting January 1, 2027, standard pricing of $1.5 / $7.5 per 1M tokens input / output will apply.

key_facts.fact: Google says 3.8 Flash scores 54.9% on HLE-Verified and outperforms most larger frontier models on DeepSWE v1.1, a long-horizon software engineering benchmark, at a fraction of the cost.
key_facts.excerpt: On DeepSWE v1.1 (Long-Horizon Software Engineering) 3.8 Flash outperforms most larger frontier models in autonomously solving complex engineering problems end to end, only at a fraction of the cost... 3.8 Flash also achieves a 54.9% on HLE-Verified.

key_facts.fact: Google says the gains came partly from long-running agentic loops that recursively evaluate and refine the underlying models, and from rigorous training in cybersecurity.
key_facts.excerpt: both of today's releases are powered by the same foundational intelligence, and further accelerated by long-running agentic loops designed to recursively evaluate and refine the underlying models.

key_facts.fact: On the internal multi-language vulnerability benchmark spanning 20 programming languages, Flash Cyber exceeds a 70% success rate; on CWE-Bench patching it reaches 47.2% pass@1 versus 47.8% for a leading frontier model at significantly lower cost.
key_facts.excerpt: the model showcases an impressive leap over our previous models and reaches a success rate exceeding 70%... Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber is on the Pareto frontier: with a pass@1 of 47.2% compared to a leading frontier model at 47.8%, yet offered at a significantly lower cost.

key_facts.fact: Google's Chrome Security team found Flash Cyber produced 2.6 times more correct patches to Chrome vulnerabilities than the best commercial models, which are much larger.
key_facts.excerpt: The Chrome Security team found that 3.8 Flash Cyber produced 2.6 times more correct patches to vulnerabilities in Chrome than the best commercial models that are much larger.

stories.headline: Cognition nears $1B raise at $47B valuation, up 81% from May, with ~$10B in demand

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on September 2, 2026 that AI coding startup Cognition is set to close a round of about $1 billion that would value it at roughly $47 billion, with talks ongoing and terms still subject to change.
key_facts.excerpt: Artificial intelligence coding startup Cognition AI Inc. is set to close a new round of funding that would vault its valuation to about $47 billion... The company is raising around $1 billion in its latest haul.

key_facts.fact: The final raise may exceed $1 billion: Cognition received nearly $10 billion in investor interest, roughly ten times the supply.
key_facts.excerpt: The final raise size may exceed that amount as Cognition fields outsize demand for the round, one of the people said, adding that Cognition received nearly $10 billion in investor interest.

key_facts.fact: The price marks an 81% jump in just over three months: Cognition raised more than $1 billion at a $26 billion post-money valuation on May 27, led by Lux Capital, General Catalyst and 8VC.
key_facts.excerpt: The proposed financing would arrive just over three months after Cognition raised more than $1 billion at a $26 billion post-money valuation on May 27th. Lux Capital, General Catalyst and 8VC led that round.

key_facts.fact: Annualized revenue has more than doubled since the May round, passing $900 million from $492 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Annualised revenue has more than doubled since May, climbing from $492 million to over $900 million.

key_facts.fact: Investor appetite was partly stoked by SpaceX's $60 billion acquisition of rival Cursor, which reset valuation benchmarks for AI coding tools.
key_facts.excerpt: Investor demand has reportedly hit nearly $10 billion, partly fuelled by SpaceX's closed $60 billion acquisition of rival Cursor.

key_facts.fact: Cognition, founded in late 2023 by Scott Wu, Steven Hao and Walden Yan, makes Devin, an autonomous software engineering agent, and bought the Windsurf coding editor in July 2025; at the May round it said Devin wrote 89% of its own code, up from 13% in December 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Cognition was founded in late 2023 by Scott Wu, Steven Hao, and Walden Yan... At the May raise, Cognition disclosed that Devin was already writing 89% of the company's own code, up from 13% in December 2025.

stories.headline: Fei-Fei Li's World Labs unveils Atlas, a world model with native camera control and 3D output

key_facts.fact: World Labs introduced Atlas on September 1, 2026, describing it as an 'omni model' pretrained from scratch to operate natively on text, images, video and 3D — a multimodal autoregressive diffusion transformer that combines all inputs into a shared spatial context.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we are introducing Atlas, our next-generation world model. Atlas is an omni model that we pretrained from scratch to natively operate on text, images, video, and 3D. It is a multimodal autoregressive diffusion transformer: all inputs are combined into a shared spatial context.

key_facts.fact: Atlas generates images and video from one or more input images with pixel-perfect camera control, outputting up to one minute of video at 1440p.
key_facts.excerpt: Camera-Controlled Generation: Atlas generates images and videos from one or more images with pixel-perfect camera control, outputting up to 1 minute of video at 1440p.

key_facts.fact: The key architectural choice is that camera geometry is a native input type rather than a text instruction, so a designed camera path drives generation instead of prompts like 'pan' or 'crane'.
key_facts.excerpt: Conventional video generators commonly receive camera instructions through text prompts such as pan, crane or truck. Atlas receives a camera path as native model input, giving users direct control over the position and angle of generated views.

key_facts.fact: Atlas reconstructs real scenes from as few as two or three images and exports explicit 3D as point clouds or Gaussian splats; World Labs says it outperforms specialized open-source reconstruction models despite being a general model.
key_facts.excerpt: Atlas typically gives faithful reconstructions with as few as two or three images, outperforming state-of-the-art results by models specially trained only for 3D reconstruction... Atlas is an omni model which performs both generation and reconstruction. Despite its generality, Atlas outperforms the best specialized open-source reconstruction models.

key_facts.fact: A robotics 'real-to-sim' use case is the stated target: World Labs shows environments reconstructed from 24 frames of phone video, then rendered as the RGB and depth a robot-mounted camera would see along a new trajectory.
key_facts.excerpt: World Labs shows large environments reconstructed from 24 frames of phone video, then viewed through simulated cameras mounted on different robot bodies. The model can generate color and depth information those cameras would see as the robot moves.

key_facts.fact: Access is limited: World Labs opened an early-access request route and has not disclosed pricing or general production availability; its published benchmarks were run in-house and gave Atlas native camera poses while competing video models got only text descriptions.
key_facts.excerpt: Early-access requests are open, but pricing and general production availability have not been disclosed... World Labs says Atlas outperforms specialized state-of-the-art models in spatial reconstruction, but the launch page does not provide a compact standardized comparison table.

stories.headline: Meta Superintelligence Labs releases Muse Voice Transcribe, its first real-time audio model

key_facts.fact: Meta Superintelligence Labs introduced Muse Voice Transcribe on September 1, 2026 — its first real-time audio perception model, delivering streaming speech recognition, speaker diarization for 20+ speakers, and endpointing.
key_facts.excerpt: We're excited to introduce Muse Voice Transcribe, the first real-time audio perception model developed by Meta Superintelligence Labs... It delivers real-time streaming ASR, diarization with 20+ speakers, and endpointing.

key_facts.fact: Meta claims first place on Artificial Analysis for streaming speech-to-text and on public diarization benchmarks, as of September 1, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: We rank first on Artificial Analysis on streaming speech-to-text and on public diarization benchmarks. Model inclusion and rankings as of September 1, 2026.

key_facts.fact: The model is autoregressive and from the Muse Spark family: it processes audio in 80ms chunks at 12.5 Hz and decides at each chunk whether to keep listening or emit a text token, using reinforcement learning to trade word error rate against delay.
key_facts.excerpt: Audio is processed in 80ms chunks (12.5 Hz), each of which is transformed into a single soft token. At each audio chunk, the model decides to either continue listening to the next audio chunk or emit a text token... This is enabled with reinforcement learning (RL), where word error rate (WER) reward and a delay reward are combined multiplicatively.

key_facts.fact: It was trained on 70+ languages, of which 25 are extensively verified, supports arbitrary code-switching within or between sentences, and natively handles audio over one hour long with no post-processing.
key_facts.excerpt: Muse Voice Transcribe is trained with 70+ languages, of which 25 are extensively verified... Our model natively supports long audio input exceeding one hour and up to 20+ speakers, with no required post-processing.

key_facts.fact: The model is available immediately via the Meta Model API, Meta AI for Mac and Muse Code, and now powers voice dictation across Meta AI and Muse Code.
key_facts.excerpt: With one click, voice dictation across Meta AI and Muse Code is now powered by Muse Voice Transcribe... Muse Voice Transcribe is available today via Meta Model API, Meta AI for Mac, and Muse Code.

stories.headline: New York City bans AI for public school students through 8th grade, the widest US moratorium

key_facts.fact: New York City Public Schools confirmed a ban on student-facing artificial intelligence for grades 2-K through eighth for the 2026-2027 academic year, affecting more than half a million students in the nation's largest school district.
key_facts.excerpt: New York City Public Schools is banning more than half a million students from using artificial intelligence for the 2026-2027 academic year... The nation's largest school district said it will begin the school year next week with a sweeping ban on AI for students in 2-K through eighth grade.

key_facts.fact: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the city is imposing a moratorium on generative AI for pre-school through eighth grade and will spend the next year studying the technology's impacts; the district calls it the most expansive AI moratorium in the nation and it also bans companion chatbots.
key_facts.excerpt: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said that the city is implementing a moratorium on generative AI for students in pre-school or 2-K through eighth grade and will spend the next year 'studying the impacts of this technology.' The district said it is implementing the most expansive AI moratorium in the nation, eliminating software that uses student-facing AI and banning companion chatbots.

key_facts.fact: The rules also cap screen time: no individual devices for pre-K through second grade, 30 minutes recommended for grades 3-5 and 45 minutes for middle schoolers.
key_facts.excerpt: The guidelines bar schools from giving individual devices to students in preschools through second grade, though classrooms will be allowed to have smart boards, sources said. For students in grades 3 to 5, the policy recommends limiting screen time on individual devices to 30 minutes and 45 minutes for middle school students.

key_facts.fact: High schoolers get restricted access — including five pilot programs and uses for literacy and career readiness — plus twice-yearly AI literacy classes; teachers may use AI for lesson prep but not to grade assignments.
key_facts.excerpt: Two-thirds of all students won't be able to use AI until high school. There will also be limits on how much time all students will be able to spend on screens, sources said. Educators will also face restrictions, as teachers will not be able to use AI to grade assignments.

key_facts.fact: The policy reverses a March 2026 framework that used a traffic-light system to classify AI tasks, which parents and teachers attacked as too lenient; a task force will produce a report in April to guide future policy.
key_facts.excerpt: The new rules follow an initial framework published in March, which used a traffic light system to determine which tasks AI would be used for. The framework... sparked fury among many parents and teachers who considered it too lenient... The task force is to produce a report in April.

key_facts.fact: Mayor Mamdani and Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels announced the policy on the morning of September 2, days before the city's school year begins on September 10.
key_facts.excerpt: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels are expected to make the announcement Wednesday morning... The announcement comes just days before the start of the new school year for the city on Sept. 10.
